objective:
Data files from other tools are sometimes broken, and the `csv` module silently guesses. Add a module `stockroom/strictcsv.py` with a strict reader that says exactly where a file is broken, and its canonical writer, and a `lint` command. `class CsvSyntaxError(ParseError)` (a subclass of `stockroom.errors.ParseError`) has attributes `line` and `column` (both 1-based integers), and its message is `line L, column C: REASON`. `parse_csv(text, *, delimiter=',') -> list[list[str]]`. The delimiter must be one character other than `"`, ``, `
` and U+FEFF; anything else raises `ValueError`. One leading U+FEFF is removed first and is not counted in columns (a second one is data). A line end is `
`, `
` or a lone ``, freely mixed. The grammar: records separated by line ends, an optional line end after the last record; a record is fields separated by the delimiter. A field is quoted when its first character is `"`: it runs to the next `"` that is not doubled, `""` inside it stands for one `"`, and the delimiter, ``, `
` and `
` inside it are data kept exactly as written; after its closing quote the next character must be the delimiter, a line end or the end of the text. Any other field is unquoted: every character up to the next delimiter, line end or end of text, taken as it is (no trimming; spaces, U+00A0, U+2028, U+0085 and form feed are ordinary data), and it may not contain `"`. A line with no characters at all where a record would start is skipped (so the only way to write a record of one empty field is `""`); the empty text gives `[]`. Every record must have as many fields as the first record. Positions: `line` counts physical lines of the text after the BOM removal, so every line end counts, also one inside a quoted field (`
` counts once), and skipped lines count too; `column` counts characters from 1 within that physical line. The errors, each a `CsvSyntaxError`: a quoted field that is not closed before the end of the text is reported at the position of its opening quote; a character other than the delimiter or a line end right after a closing quote is reported at the position of that character; a `"` inside an unquoted field (that is, not as the field's first character, including after leading spaces) is reported at the position of that `"`; a record with a different number of fields is reported at the line where the record starts, column 1, with the reason `expected N fields, found M`. The text is read from start to end and the first error met is reported; a record's number of fields is checked when that record ends, before the next record is read. `format_csv(rows, *, delimiter=',', line_end='
') -> str` takes any iterable of sequences of strings and writes each record followed by `line_end`, which must be `
`, `
` or `` (otherwise `ValueError`; the delimiter is checked as in `parse_csv`). A field is quoted (wrapped in `"`, with every `"` inside doubled) exactly when it contains the delimiter, `"`, `` or `
`, when it starts with U+FEFF, or when it is empty and the only field of its record; every other field is written as it is. A record with no fields, or rows of different lengths, raise `ValueError`; no rows give `''`. For every list of rows that `format_csv` accepts and every delimiter and line end, `parse_csv(format_csv(rows, ...), delimiter=...) == rows`, also with the final line end removed or a U+FEFF put in front, and `format_csv(parse_csv(text))` of a written text gives it back. Finally add `python -m stockroom lint FILE [--delimiter D] [--out OUT]`. It reads FILE as UTF-8 bytes without any newline translation (a line end inside a quoted field must survive exactly), parses it with `parse_csv` and prints one line: `N records of M fields`, with `record` and `field` in the singular for 1 (`1 record of 1 field`), or `0 records` for a file without records. With `--out` it writes `format_csv(rows)` (default delimiter and `
`) as UTF-8 to OUT, without a BOM and without newline translation. `D` is the single delimiter character (a tab is passed as a real tab character). A syntax error, a file that is not valid UTF-8 or a delimiter that `parse_csv` refuses exits with code 1, `stockroom: error: ` followed by the error message on stderr (for a syntax error the message is the `CsvSyntaxError` message), empty stdout and no OUT file. Existing behaviour otherwise stays.
